results.reasoning: Judged headless on the scratch copy sitting-0914: a throwaway copy of its blueprint was registered ephemerally as `lint-probe` in the copy's own home (probe-import.txt), edited (probe-edits.diff) and linted with `node bin/walkdown.js lint --blueprint lint-probe --no-checks`, then forgotten and deleted. Baseline lint of the untouched copy raised no length finding (lint-baseline.txt). With edits: a 50-word one-sentence statement and a 40-word because on ownership.authoring.steps-are-required drew `statement-reads-as-a-paragraph` ("the statement is 50 words in 1 sentence(s) — say the goal in one breath and let the steps carry the rest") and `because-carries-history` ("a reason is timeless; what happened, with its date or count, belongs in `history:`") — each says what the field is for, not only the number crossed; a 9-word three-sentence statement drew the paragraph warning on sentence count alone; a 45-word one-sentence statement with a 35-word because, and a 44-word two-sentence statement, stayed silent even though those same rules carried stale-steps errors and drift warnings. All three findings are level `warn` in the JSON (lint-probe.json); the only errors were pre-existing tracking errors plus the stale-steps the edits themselves caused. The tagged test in test/lint.test.js passes (lint-tests.txt, 21/21).
